race.name: GFNY Cali
race.tagline: A 100-mile Colombian race across sugar-cane flats and Andean foothills, with 1,653 meters of climbing and tropical heat.

vitals.start_format: Mass-start competitive long course with chip timing
vitals.registration: Online through the official GFNY race site
vitals.feed_zones: Official GFNY aid stations with hydration, food, technical, and medical support
vitals.cutoff_time: See current race guide and official course rules
route_options: Recreational medium route: see official race site

climate.description: Cali sits around 1,000 meters above sea level and remains warm year-round. July is often relatively dry, but strong sun, humidity, valley wind, and afternoon weather remain real factors.

terrain.primary: Fast valley roads with long rolling and climbing sectors
terrain.surface: Paved urban, agricultural, and foothill roads across the Valle del Cauca.
features: A fast urban rollout from Avenida Sexta
Wind-exposed sugar-cane flats across the Cauca River valley
Rolling and climbing roads at the edge of the Andes

fondo_rating.scoring_notes: Century distance, a varied valley-to-foothills course, and Cali's cycling culture produce a high Tier 2 score. Inaugural operations and limited event prestige prevent Tier 1.

key_climbs: A fast urban rollout from Avenida Sexta
Wind-exposed sugar-cane flats across the Cauca River valley
Rolling and climbing roads at the edge of the Andes
climb_profile.profile_type: Fast valley roads with long rolling and climbing sectors
climb_profile.king_of_mountain: The transition from the sugar-cane flats to the Andean foothills, when early group speed must become controlled climbing durability.

course_description.character: GFNY Cali uses the flat speed of the Cauca River valley to stretch the field before accumulating 1,653 meters of elevation on a full 160.8-kilometer route. Wind, mid-altitude heat, and the ability to keep climbing after a fast opening define the race.
course_description.signature_challenge: The transition from the sugar-cane flats to the Andean foothills, when early group speed must become controlled climbing durability.

logistics.airport: Alfonso Bonilla Aragón International Airport (CLO) is about 14 kilometers northeast of Cali and has domestic and international service.
logistics.lodging_strategy: Stay near Chipichape or central north Cali for race-week access. Confirm secure bike storage and allow time for city traffic.
logistics.transport: Use official race-week instructions for packet pickup, start access, and bike transport.
logistics.food: Cali offers rice, plantain, soups, grilled meats, fruit, and abundant cafes. Practice the same high-carbohydrate intake the 100-mile race will require.

history.origin_story: GFNY announced Cali in July 2026 as its second new Colombian event for 2027, centered on a 160.8-kilometer valley-and-foothills course.
history.reputation: A high-potential inaugural century in one of Colombia's strongest cycling cities, awaiting proof of operations and field depth.

biased_opinion.summary: GFNY Cali uses the flat speed of the Cauca River valley to stretch the field before accumulating 1,653 meters of elevation on a full 160.8-kilometer route. Wind, mid-altitude heat, and the ability to keep climbing after a fast opening define the race.
weaknesses: Heat and wind can flatten tactical nuance
The new event lacks historical field depth
biased_opinion.bottom_line: A properly long new GFNY that asks for speed, climbing durability, and heat management in equal measure.

final_verdict.one_liner: A 100-mile Colombian race across sugar-cane flats and Andean foothills, with 1,653 meters of climbing and tropical heat.
final_verdict.should_you_race: A properly long new GFNY that asks for speed, climbing durability, and heat management in equal measure.
final_verdict.alternatives: GFNY Villavicencio for a shorter Colombian race with a sharper mountain selector, or GFNY NYC for established global prestige.
